scope_statement: Each ground-reaction topic raised by the #8493 chapter is mapped to the original works already adjudicated in external_source_review.json. Works are deduplicated once and may inform several topics; reuse across topics is not replication. Topic gaps are recorded as declared scope limits, never closed by adding an unverified reference.

corpus_access.method: notebooklm auth check --test --json against the local default profile
corpus_access.credential_handling: No cookie, bearer token, storage-state file, password, or session artifact is copied into this repository. The observed booleans above are the tool's own status report.
corpus_access.unblock_action: A human must run notebooklm login and complete Google authentication interactively. Passwords, second factors, CAPTCHA, and browser authentication dialogs are not automated.
corpus_access.consequence: Notebook and source-inventory identifiers cannot be recorded on this date. The corpus is a lead index only, so its absence removes a search aid and does not withdraw support from any topic below.

evidence_policy.verification_rule: Every work below was checked against its own DOI, PubMed or PMC record, or publisher record before use, and carries the boundary registered for it in external_source_review.json.
evidence_policy.gap_rule: A topic gap is closed only by an independently verified original source that the article also cites; it is never closed by a generated summary or by an uncited bibliography addition.

works.verification_method: PubMed record and Crossref relation metadata reviewed for the retained-study count, terminology finding, and correction status.
works.contribution: Systematic review of golf ground-reaction force and centre-of-pressure measurement, reporting inconsistent terminology and method across the retained studies.
works.boundary: A synthesis, not a substitute for the underlying primary studies, and no cited study identifies a unique biological command, universal COP waveform, or causal performance intervention.

works.verification_method: Publisher record resolved from the DOI and reviewed for the participant count, joint-level agreement, and transfer-magnitude statements.
works.contribution: Segment energy generation, absorption, and transfer balance applied to sagittal walking data, with intersegment transfer comparable in magnitude to generation and absorption.
works.boundary: Two participants, sagittal walking, and reported disagreement at the ankle during weight acceptance and late push-off; not golf validation and not muscle identification.

works.verification_method: PubMed record reviewed for the input-variable expansion, participant count, and force-plate reference measurement.
works.contribution: Neural-network recovery of six-axis ground reactions from plantar-pressure inputs validated against force plates, establishing that pressure instrumentation yields predicted rather than measured shear and moment channels.
works.boundary: The nonvertical channels are model predictions in the reported sample and apparatus; the method does not make free moment a directly measured insole observable.

works.verification_method: Publisher record resolved from the DOI and reviewed for the residual-reduction parameter scope and validation task.
works.contribution: Automated optimization of OpenSim residual-reduction parameters, documenting how dynamic inconsistency between measured contact and modelled dynamics is reduced.
works.boundary: Reduces and documents residuals in the reported task; it does not turn a residual into a measurement of unmodelled muscle action.

works.verification_method: Publisher record resolved from the DOI and reviewed for the induced-acceleration and power-transfer definitions used in the article.
works.contribution: Definitions separating net joint power from muscle-induced acceleration and power, and the simulation requirements each analysis family imposes.
works.boundary: Induced quantities depend on coordinates, constraints, actuator representation, state, and intervention definition, and do not uniquely identify neural control.

works.verification_method: PubMed record reviewed for the participant count, skill span, and cluster-analysis result.
works.contribution: Cluster analysis of centre-of-pressure patterns in 62 golfers spanning professional through high-handicap levels, yielding two recurring direction-of-hit patterns.
works.boundary: A description of recurring patterns in one sample; it does not claim that two clusters exhaust two-dimensional COP behaviour.

works.verification_method: PubMed record and publisher record reviewed for the participant count, handicap ceiling, club conditions, and association-only framing.
works.contribution: Associations between selected lead- and trail-foot force and moment parameters and maximum clubhead speed in 63 highly skilled male golfers across three club conditions.
works.boundary: Association only, male low-handicap population, selected peaks and club conditions, no causal intervention and no energetic source attribution.

works.verification_method: Open-access publisher record resolved from the DOI and reviewed for the joint inertial-parameter and kinematics adjustment scope.
works.contribution: Automated scaling, inverse kinematics, and inverse dynamics that jointly adjust inertial parameters and kinematics to reduce dynamic inconsistency.
works.boundary: A processing pipeline validated on its own corpus; it does not validate the golf reaction decomposition committed here.

works.verification_method: Open-access publisher article reviewed for the sample size, pooled club conditions, regression blocks, and mediation design.
works.contribution: Hierarchical regression and mediation on 30 golfers in which centre-of-pressure factors plus skill group explain part of clubhead-speed variance and a constructed impulse-related transfer factor carries an indirect association.
works.boundary: Small sample relative to the upstream feature space, pooled clubs, constructed factors, observational mediation, and no longitudinal causal intervention.

works.verification_method: PubMed record reviewed for the participant count and the handicap, club, and footwear conditions.
works.contribution: Shoe-to-natural-turf torque measured in 24 golfers across handicap, club, and footwear conditions, the closest cited measurement of a rotational foot-surface interface load.
works.boundary: An interface torque under specified footwear and surface conditions; it is not a free moment transported to a declared centre of pressure.

topics.question: Which original human measurements bound the article's treatment of centre-of-pressure trajectories and their association with clubhead speed?
gaps: No cited original source establishes a universal centre-of-pressure waveform, so the article registers COP as a described observable rather than a control variable.
disagreements: Ball and Best describe two recurring direction-of-hit clusters while Ratchanavy and colleagues represent COP as principal-component factors inside a mediation model. The article treats these as non-equivalent descriptions and adopts neither as a canonical COP parameterization.

topics.question: Which original sources qualify the foot-ground contact representation used to convert modelled reactions into bilateral loads?
gaps: No cited original source qualifies a compliant or friction-cone foot-ground contact model for the golf swing.
The committed benchmark uses a fixed support with no feet, so bilateral foot-force allocation, centre of pressure, and free moment stay registered as non-identifiable instead of being modelled.
disagreements: The residual-reduction literature treats dynamic inconsistency as a quantity to minimize, whereas this article treats an inverse-dynamics residual as unidentified by construction. The article keeps the stricter reading and does not report reduced residuals as evidence of recovered contact loads.

topics.question: Which original sources bound the article's derivation and use of the vertical free moment about a transported centre of pressure?
gaps: No cited original source reports a golf free moment transported to a declared centre of pressure; the shoe-surface torque measurement is a related but distinct interface observable.

The wrench-transport convention that defines centre of pressure and the residual vertical free moment is derived in the article from rigid-body statics rather than adopted from a cited measurement standard.
disagreements: Pressure-instrumented work reports six-axis reactions recovered by a trained model, which the article declines to treat as a direct free-moment measurement.

topics.question: Which original human measurements bound the article's use of golf ground-reaction force magnitude, direction, and timing, and the prospective test it registers?
gaps: No cited study releases participant-level six-axis bilateral wrench time series that this article could independently re-analyze, so the prospective falsification protocol stays registered rather than executed.
disagreements: Han and colleagues report skill-associated force and moment peaks in a low-handicap male sample, while the 2026 systematic review reports that terminology and reporting differ across the retained studies. The article adopts the review's caution rather than any single peak convention.

topics.question: Which original sources bound the segment energy generation, absorption, and transfer language the ground-reaction attribution borrows?
gaps: Neither source is a golf measurement, so segment-power transfer during the swing remains model-internal and inherits no human validation from them.
disagreements: A Robertson-Winter segment energy balance and a Zajac induced-acceleration analysis answer different questions. The article keeps both and does not report a joint-power balance as an induced-power attribution.

inference_boundary: This reconciliation cannot show that the ground-reaction attribution is correct for a human golfer. It records which original sources bound each topic and which questions no cited source answers; the enumerated NotebookLM corpus is unavailable on the recorded date and would in any case only supply leads.
